newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico inflation slowdown welcomed by analysts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico inflation slowdown welcomed by analysts.

text.p: Analysts on Monday welcomed Mexico's May consumer inflation data, which showed a monthly rise of less than one percent for the first time since a devastating peso crash in December 1994.

Earlier, the central bank said consumer prices rose 0.91 percent in May after a 1.08 percent increase in April. The May figure was a tick lower than the average forecast of 0.92 percent in a Reuter survey of analysts' forecasts.
Mexico's producer price index rose 0.69 percent in May after a rise of 0.70 percent in April.

"The data is good. It confirms the tendency is still downwards," said Pedro Alonso, an economic analyst at brokerage Inverlat in Mexico City. He said Mexico usually experienced its weakest inflation in June and July.
"It's the lowest since November 1994," said Eduardo Estrada, deputy director of financial analysis at Bancomer in Mexico City. "Our forecast for the next month is again below one percent."
Analysts at MMS said it appeared inflation would stay benign throughout the summer, though the rate may have already touched its lowest point.
Estrada said the slowing of inflation in part reflected a steady peso.

"One quite important factor has been stability in the nominal exchange rate," he said. "We expect a little turmoil after the elections, and we expect a little rebound in inflation in August and September."
Mexicans go to the polls on July 6 to elect a new lower house, part of the senate, six state governors and, for the first time, Mexico City's mayor.

Analysts say uncertainty surrounding the election, when the Institutional Revolutionary Party may lose its majority in Congress for the first time in 68 years, could provoke some uneasiness on the foreign exchange market.
That combined with seasonal factors in the holiday and back-to-school months of August and September may well push inflation back over the one percent level.
Bancomer is looking for inflation of over one percent in August. Prices in September may rise by up to 1.3 percent, it says.
In a preliminary forecast, Inverlat said it was expecting inflation of just under one percent in August and possibly 1.14 percent in September.

Estrada said the slower rise in prices in May also reflected stability in central bank policy, despite persistent strength in the monetary base, which has prompted talk the bank is fuelling economic growth ahead of the elections.

But Estrada said any pump-priming would have shown up in the May inflation data. Strength of the monetary base was probably linked at least in part to remonetarisation of the Mexican economy, he said.
Banco de Mexico said the 0.91 percent CPI rise was made up of increases in household utilities, housing rents and some food and household products.

The May rise took cumulative inflation for the year to 7.71 percent, compared with 13.46 percent in the year-earlier period. In May, the basic basket of consumer goods climbed 0.79 percent from April.
Official forecasts for the full year call for inflation at 15 percent. Analysts say 17 to 18 percent is more likely. ((--Mexico City newsroom +525 729 7905))
